q: Three Lewis structures for dinitrogen monoxide (laughing gas, N<sub>2</sub>O) are drawn below. Which of them are resonance structures of one another?
h: Resonance structures keep every atom in the same position and differ only in where the electrons (lone pairs and multiple bonds) are placed.
w: I and II both have the N–N–O arrangement and differ only in electron placement, so I and II only are resonance structures. III has N–O–N connectivity, a different arrangement of atoms, so it is not a resonance form of the others.
x: III has the atoms in a different order (N–O–N), so it isn't a resonance form.
III has a different arrangement of atoms.
III has a different arrangement of atoms.

q: The table lists the quantum numbers of four electrons in the same atom. Which two electrons occupy the SAME orbital?
h: An orbital is fixed by n, ℓ and m<sub>ℓ</sub>. Two electrons share an orbital only if those three match and their spins differ.
w: Electrons I and II both have (n, ℓ, mℓ) = (2, 1, 0) — the same 2p orbital — and opposite spins, as Pauli requires. I and III are both 2p electrons but in different 2p orbitals (mℓ = 0 vs 1); IV is in the 2s orbital (ℓ = 0). 'Same subshell' is not the same as 'same orbital'.
x: I and III are in different 2p orbitals (m_ℓ = 0 vs 1).
IV is in the 2s orbital (ℓ = 0), while III is a 2p electron (ℓ = 1). Electrons in the same orbital must match in n, ℓ and m<sub>ℓ</sub>, differing only in spin.
II and IV are in different subshells.

q: Protons, neutrons and electrons are tabulated for species I–IV. Which pair of entries are ISOTOPES of one element?
h: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. Electron count does not matter for this.
w: Species I and II both have 17 protons (chlorine) with 18 and 20 neutrons: Cl-35 and Cl-37 (II happens to be the Cl− ion, which does not change the element). II and III have the same MASS NUMBER (37) but different elements; III and IV share 18 electrons (isoelectronic), not the same element; I and IV differ in protons.
x: II and III have the same mass number but are different elements.
III and IV have the same electrons but different elements.
I and IV have different numbers of protons.
